mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Velar P300 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Range Rover Velar P300 typically ranges from £4,200 to £6,500 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £1,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing PT204 engine in a Range Rover Velar P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Range Rover Velar P300 are unexplained coolant loss, a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts (timing chain rattle), or illuminated temperature warning lights. You should also check for sweet-smelling exhaust or oil residue around the valve cover.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Velar P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A typical Range Rover Velar P300 holds a UK market value of £18,000-£50,000, making a £4,200-£6,500 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, refinement, and strong resale value for years to come.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Velar P300 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover Velar P300 typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Range Rover Velar P300 and the P250 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Range Rover Velar P300 uses a higher-output tune of the 2.0-litre turbocharged inline-4 petrol engine (PT204) producing 300 PS, prioritising smooth, responsive performance. In contrast, the P250 uses the same base architecture but is tuned to 250 PS, offering slightly better fuel economy at the expense of outright acceleration.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Velar P300 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Range Rover Velar launched in 2017, the P300 badge introduced a refined, high-output 2.0-litre turbocharged Ingenium petrol engine, offering a smooth and responsive alternative to the diesel lineup for the premium compact SUV.

milestones.description: Introduction of the PT204 2.0L turbocharged inline-4 petrol engine (300 PS / 296 hp) in the Velar P300, featuring a twin-scroll turbocharger and direct injection.
2023 - Minor ECU calibration updates and the introduction of a critical cooling system recall to address potential fire risks, improving long-term safety without altering the core PT204 architecture.
present - Continued production with refined engine management software for the L560 facelift, maintaining the P300's position as a balanced performance option.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover Velar P300 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure & Fire Risk Recall - Why the Range Rover Velar P300 PT204 Overheats
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Unpredictable (recall affects 2017-2023 production regardless of mileage)
problems.rootCause: Coolant system component failure causes rapid overheating and pressurisation, leading to coolant ejection and a documented engine fire risk, prompting a formal JLR recall.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant pump, expansion tank, hoses, and update ECU software.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for proactive prevention before catastrophic failure occurs.

repairOptions.longevity: Required if the engine has already suffered catastrophic overheating or fire damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Velar P300 of relevant age (2017-present) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £18,000-£50,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Cazoo market observations]. At this premium value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and easily justifies the investment to preserve performance and resale value.
problems.recommendation: If you own a 2017-2023 petrol Velar, verify the cooling system recall has been completed immediately. If your Range Rover Velar P300 is exhibiting minor coolant seepage but has not suffered thermal damage, a targeted preventative cooling system refresh by a JLR specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has overheated, a full rebuilt replacement is the only reliable long-term solution.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the Range Rover Velar P300 PT204 Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Over time, the timing chain tensioners can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch and produce a characteristic rattling noise on cold starts. If ignored, this can lead to catastrophic internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip front covers, replace timing chain, guides and updated tensioner assembly.
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive fix for chain rattle; prevents catastrophic valve-to-piston contact if addressed promptly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded valvetrain components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if chain failure has already caused internal engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the £18,000-£50,000 value of a Range Rover Velar P300 makes targeted repairs like a timing chain refresh highly viable. A full engine replacement is rarely justified for chain rattle alone unless secondary damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle in your Range Rover Velar P300. A timely chain and tensioner replacement by a specialist is a well-documented fix that preserves the engine's longevity at a fraction of the cost of a full rebuild.
